To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a novel nanoscale assembly of gold nanoparticles with the potential for brain tumor targeting.

we developed an effective strategy to enhance the retention of nanoparticles in the brain tumor microenvironment by the assembly of nanoparticles into nanoassemblies and the dynamic switching between the nanoassemblies and single nanoparticles in response to the microenvironment.
we report the self-assembly of gold nanoparticles into nanoassemblies for enhanced brain tumor targeting and therapeutic efficacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-assembly of gold nanoparticles into nanoassemblies as a drug delivery system for the treatment of brain tumors.
the development of a novel drug delivery strategy for brain tumor targeting.
the development of gold nanoparticles for the delivery of anticancer drug to brain tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanoassemblies of gold nanoparticles are a promising nanoplatform for brain tumor therapy with enhanced targeting and bioelimination.
the nanoassemblies have been successfully designed and fabricated for brain tumor treatment, and their therapeutic efficacy is significantly higher than the conventional nanoparticles.
the self-assembly of nanoparticles into larger nanospheres provides an effective strategy for enhanced tumor targeting and bioelimination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a novel nanoassembly of gold nanoparticles that can target the brain tumors, and the assembly can be switched into single gold nanoparticle by intracellular redox environment, which is a promising approach to improve the brain tumor treatment.
the size of nanoparticles can be controlled and tuned by self-assembly of single nanoparticles into larger nanostructures.

the size and morphology of gold nanoassemblies can be controlled by the self-assembly of the single gold nanoparticles, which can be used as a drug delivery system with the capability of dynamic switching and targeting to brain tumor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assembly of gold nanostructures into larger nanoassemblies provides a new approach for the design of multifunctional nanomedicine for brain tumor treatment.
the assembly of nanoparticles into nanospheres can be used to improve tumor targeting and bioelimination.
the assembly of nanoparticles can be a promising strategy to overcome biological barriers and enhance the therapeutic efficacy of the nanoparticle formulations.
